reason: The backend sizes a box for a text and the client draws that text inside it, so both tiers must estimate a text's width one way (backend-centralization R10). The width of a text is its characters times the font size times the average advance: characters x fontSize x averageAdvance, with averageAdvance fixed at 0.55 and 14 the font size the four measuring modules (ansible-structure, c4, causal-loop, mindmap) use today. A character is a UTF-16 code unit, which is what .NET's string.Length and JavaScript's string.length both count, so a character outside the Basic Multilingual Plane counts as two on both tiers; the emoji case pins that. Spaces are characters like any other. This is the metric only: the padding, minimum and maximum a module adds around it to size a box stay each module's own declared values (R10.2), so no case here includes them. Widths are written as the decimal the formula means; floating point makes 1 x 14 x 0.55 come out as 7.700000000000001, so both suites compare within 'tolerance' rather than exactly.
